scenes.narration: AI forgets the start of very long chats.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson eight. In under a minute, you'll learn why that happens.
A context window is the amount of text a model can look at all at once, measured in tokens.
scenes.definition: The amount of text a model can look at at once, measured in tokens.

scenes.narration: Think of a whiteboard on your desk. It only fits so much. Keep writing, and the oldest lines have to be erased to make room.
scenes.label: Only so much fits
scenes.sub: Write more, and old lines get erased.
scenes.note: A window is a fixed size

scenes.narration: Everything shares one window: the instructions, your earlier messages, your new question, and even the space the answer needs. When it's full, older text may get cut.
scenes.footer: Full window, old text gets cut

scenes.narration: Here's how it looks. Early on, you mention your dog's name. Much later, after the window fills up, the AI no longer sees it, and can't answer.

messages.text: My dog is Biscuit. ... Hundreds of messages later ... What's my dog's name?
I don't see a name in our conversation. Could you remind me?

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: the context window is how much text a model sees at once. Two: it's measured in tokens. Three: when it fills up, older text can be cut.
points: Context window = text seen at once
When full, older text can be cut
